literature_lessons_for_date_table: Prosperity and Phi show both a dense weak baseline and stronger sparse baselines; their strongest defensible headline is tied to PTB or Stellar, not the dense multiplier.
Bishop obtains a large strong-baseline end-to-end number by matching PTB resources and accelerating projection, MLP and attention together with algorithm/hardware co-design.
All three use an executable architecture/runtime model and separately report layer/ablation numbers; none licenses converting a source-work ratio directly into cycle speedup.

Our defensible strong-baseline result today is 1.156371355x on four bottleneck Conv operators. A projected 10.340668x versus dense16 may be shown only as a secondary weak-baseline column after formal replay.
